subject: Brightlane DPA: role mapping and SCCs — coordination and timeline

Subject: DPA redline from Brightlane (first pass)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — Brightlane is keen to move forward. Attached is our first-pass redline to the proposed DPA and a separate spreadsheet showing where our data is routed (for the transfer impact assessment).

High-level asks:
- We marked Redwood as "processor" but requested a narrow subprocessor consent flow (section 3.2) — Brightlane legal prefers explicit notice + 10 business day objection window.
- We proposed an expanded SCC schedule to reflect our hybrid processing model (US + EU).
- We also added an indemnity carveout for unlawful data transfers (see §8).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a sample transfer impact addendum (TIA) or a short annex with subprocessors and data center locations? We need this for our procurement and privacy teams.

Best,
Oliver Brooks
Head of Legal Ops, Brightlane Health

Attachment: Brightlane_DPA_redline_20260801.docx (redline, tracked changes)
Attachment: data_flow_locations.xlsx (processor location export)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline from Brightlane (first pass)

Thanks for the ping, Lauren. Reviewed Brightlane's redline — a few preliminary notes and suggested language below. I attached an excerpt with inline comments.

Summary of legal positions (high level):
- Subprocessor objection window: we should avoid a hard 10-business-day veto. Proposed compromise: written notice + 10-business-day "quiet period" where Brightlane may raise objections and Redwood will evaluate materiality. For high-risk subprocessors (per role map) we can offer a 10-business-day notice and the option to pause onboarding pending remediation or alternative routing.
- SCCs: we will adopt the EU Commission's 2021 SCCs where applicable. We need Brown/IT to confirm which processing activities are "controller-to-processor" vs "processor-to-processor" (impacts Annex I/II mapping). Propose including a short table in the annex rather than reauthoring SCC text.
- Indemnity for unlawful transfers: we can accept a narrowly tailored carveout limited to willful misconduct or gross negligence in transfers; we will not accept open-ended transfer indemnities.
- Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): Redwood has a standard TIA template; I'll produce a version for Brightlane that references our published subprocessor list and the regional hosting summary. That should satisfy procurement.

Action items I need:
- Lauren/Monica: confirm which deployment this deal will use (hosted API vs dedicated vs private). The solution impacts our risk posture and proposed SCC annex.
- Kim: any commercial constraints on objection windows or indemnity exposure (we may need a small credit holdback vs unlimited indemnity).

I'll attach: "K_Iyer_DPA_comments_20260803.docx" (excerpted comments). Planning to deliver consolidated redline tomorrow EOD.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Oliver Brooks <oliver.brooks@brightlane.com>, Emma Jones <emma.jones@brightlane.com>, contracts@brightlane.com

Date: 2026-08-04T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood consolidated DPA redline + mutual action plan

Oliver / Emma — thanks for the redline. Attaching our consolidated response and a short mutual action plan (MAP) with dates. Highlights:

- Subprocessors: We propose a notice + 10-business-day quiet period for objections; for any "high-risk" subprocessors (as defined in the annex) we will provide a more formal pause and remediation path.
- SCCs & Role Map: Attached is a one-page role map (controller/processor flows) and our proposed placement of the SCC Annex. We will adopt the 2021 SCCs and include the processor-to-processor mapping as an annex for cross-border flows.
- Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): Attached TIA-questionnaire.xlsx is our short template. We included a summary of our hosting regions and public subprocessor registry.
- Indemnity: We can accept a narrowly tailored transfer-related carveout limited to willful misconduct/gross negligence.

Proposed MAP:
- 8/4 (today) — Redwood sends consolidated redline (attached).
- 8/5 — Brightlane to review and mark up; Procurement to confirm any internal purchase order / billing requirements.
- 8/6 — Final alignment call (30 min) and DocuSign execution target by EOD 8/6.

Please confirm if Brightlane can live with the objection "quiet period" approach and the narrow indemnity carveout. If you prefer the 10-business-day veto, flag that in your reply and we will escalate to commercial for consideration.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_consolidated_redline_20260803.docx, TIA-questionnaire.xlsx

Best regards,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
